draft.title: The second derivative and concavity
card: The second derivative f''(x) is the derivative of f'(x). It tells you how the gradient is changing.
f''(x) > 0. The gradient is increasing and the curve bends upwards like a cup.
f''(x) < 0. The gradient is decreasing and the curve bends downwards like a cap.

A point of inflection is where concavity changes, so f''(x) changes sign there. Example: f(x) = x³ has f'(x) = 3x² and f''(x) = 6x. This is negative for x < 0 and positive for x > 0, so the concavity changes at x = 0.
draft.remember: Sign of f''(x) gives the concavity. A change of sign gives a point of inflection.

a.q: For f(x) = x³ − 3x², f''(x) = 6x − 6. Where is the curve concave up?
a.why: The curve is concave up where 6x − 6 > 0, which gives x > 1. The option x < 1 is tempting, but there f''(x) is negative, so the curve is concave down.

b.q: f(x) = x⁴ has f''(x) = 12x². Which statement about the point (0, 0) is true?
opts: Not an inflection point, as f''(x) does not change sign
An inflection point, as the curve is concave up
Not an inflection point, as f''(x) is negative there
b.why: f''(x) = 12x² is positive on both sides of x = 0, so the concavity does not change and there is no point of inflection. The tempting option says f''(0) = 0 is enough, but the sign of f''(x) must change.
b.clue: Check the sign of f''(x) on each side of x = 0.

b.best: Not an inflection point, as f''(x) does not change sign
